extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community (investigators, applicants, grantees, and institutional administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: A roundup of NIH Extramural Nexus news items that describe policy updates, resources, review outcomes, and procedural changes relevant to preparing and managing NIH grant applications and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate research models (New Approach Methodologies, NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance our understanding of human health and disease. As we continue to encourage approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential, investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose models that are scientifically sound and matched to the specific research question; favor approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential where appropriate. (From: 'Selecting the Right Models for Your Research: A Focus on New Approach Methodologies (NAMs)')

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects — application format and linked-award handling
rubrics_metrics.description: New Video Overview for NIH’s Collaborative International Research Projects (PF5): 6-minute overview of the new PF5 award structure to learn key features and application format and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants to PF5 should follow the specified application format, understand key features of the new award structure, and be aware that applications may be split into linked awards after peer review and before Just-in-Time (JIT) requests. (Guidance offered via the 6-minute NIH overview video.)

rubrics_metrics.name: 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format — required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: A new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format has been issued based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS Plans for NIH submissions, use the 2026 Pilot format and include the simplified set of required elements specified in that format. (Apply the new format in place of prior formats where applicable.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations for replication and reproducibility in applications and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Embedding Replication and Reproducibility Throughout NIH Research: Key Reminders for Applications, Awards, and a New Highlighted Topic. The reliability of biomedical research is foundational to public trust in science and to ensuring that findings can benefit patients and communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should explicitly consider and describe replication and reproducibility in study design, methods, and plans; NIH's 'Gold Standard Science' plan and the Replication and Reproducibility Initiative aim to drive, incentivize, and institutionalize such efforts. Use the highlighted topic and key reminders when preparing applications and award plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring outcome: 'Competitive but Not Discussed' (CBND)
rubrics_metrics.description: Following emergency modifications to review processes, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed' to recognize that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that receiving a 'competitive but not discussed' score indicates placement in the middle third of the study section and is an official review outcome reflecting review triage decisions under adjusted procedures; applicants should interpret this in the context of NIH review cutoffs and subsequent processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralization of NIH peer review at the Center for Scientific Review (CSR)
rubrics_metrics.description: All peer review was centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR). The consolidation aims to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency in the peer-review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and institutions should be aware that peer review processes and procedures are centralized at CSR; this may affect study section assignments, review timelines, and administrative processes. Consult CSR guidance and news updates for procedural details and implications for submissions.
